identification.notes: UR-protocol models (URTM*/SYWP* name prefixes) do not expose their service UUID as a constant in the app; identify them by advertised name prefix and enumerate services after connect. 0x1826 / 0xFFF0 cover the FTMS and FT classes respectively — 0xFFF0 is attributed to the FT proprietary protocol class ONLY. Whether UR-class pads advertise 0xFFF0 (or anything else) is unknown; their service and characteristic UUIDs must come from hardware capture, not from this list.

device.name: UREVO walking pad family (URTM*/SYWP* under-desk treadmills)
device.notes:
UREVO's walking pads / under-desk treadmills (model numbers seen in the app: URTM012, URTM018, URTM022, URTM023, URTM024, URTM029, URTM030, URTM041, SYWP006; retail families include SpaceWalk, Strol and CyberPad) are controlled over BLE by the official UREVO app. The manufacturer is alive and shipping; this is a cloud-independence spec: the app ties account, workout history, OTA and per-model metadata to the UREVO cloud (service.urevosports.com), while the control plane is local BLE GATT. No pairing/bonding or authentication strings exist anywhere in the treadmill code paths — control appears to be open to any central in range, as with other walking-pad brands.
The app's BLE layer routes a discovered peripheral to one of several protocol handlers. Three of them cover treadmills; the short names FTMS, FT and UR below are this spec's own labels for the three wire protocols, not the app's:
1. FTMS — standard Bluetooth Fitness
   Machine Service 0x1826. Selected when the advertisement carries
   0x1826. Characteristic set confirmed by the handler's UUID accessors:
   write 0x2AD9 (Control Point), notify 0x2ACD (Treadmill Data),
   0x2ADA (Fitness Machine Status) and 0x2AD3 (Training Status), plus
   reads of 0x2AD4 (Supported Speed Range) and 0x2AD5 (Supported
   Inclination Range). No vendor pre-amble or private characteristic
   exists in this path — treat it as plain FTMS 1.0.

2. FT proprietary — private service
   0xFFF0, write 0xFFF2, notify 0xFFF1. Speaks the Frame-A frame
   grammar (below) with command class 0x44. Model-specific subclasses
   exist in the binary (eleven of them, keyed by model) and are
   selected from per-model config.

3. UR proprietary — UREVO's own treadmill protocol, matched by
   advertised-name prefix URTM* / SYWP* at handler-selection time. Speaks the same Frame-A grammar with
   command class 0x53, plus a second frame family, Frame B,
   (0x5A 0xA5 header, >= 11 bytes) used at least for the controller
   version-info query. NOTA BENE: no GATT service/characteristic UUID
   constants exist in the binary for this class (verified 2026-08-12 by
   full string-table enumeration of the snapshot: the only 16-bit GATT
   UUIDs present are 0x180A, 0x1826, 0x2A23-0x2A29, 0x2ACD/2AD3/2AD4/
   2AD5/2AD9/2ADA, 0xFEE0-0xFEE2, 0xFFF0-0xFFF2) — the app binds the
   UR characteristics by GATT enumeration and/or per-model cloud config.
   The UR service/characteristic UUIDs must be captured
   from hardware (HCI snoop); do not guess them.

Relationship to KingSmith WalkingPad (see kingsmith-walkingpad.yaml): none at the protocol level. The KingSmith WiLink service 0xFE00, the ODM characteristic d18d2c10-… and the supplement service 24e2521c-… are all ABSENT from the UREVO binary (0 matches), and the UREVO frame grammar (02…03 + XOR-0x5A checksum; 5A A5 + CRC-16) shares nothing with WiLink (F7…FD + additive checksum). The only overlap is that both brands ship newer models speaking standard FTMS 0x1826.
The same app also drives UREVO recovery massagers (name prefix UCRM*; the vendor's own profile; services 0xFFF0 and 0xFEE0 — write 0xFEE2, notify 0xFEE1 on the V2 generation) and smart scales (the hex string 55525753 = ASCII "URWS" appears in the handler matcher). Those product lines are out of scope for this spec.
SAFETY: motorised exercise equipment. The frame grammar carries no authentication, so anyone in radio range can issue start/speed commands once the frame bytes are confirmed against hardware.
Cloud dependency: none for control once the GATT endpoints are known. The UR class's reliance on cloud per-model config for endpoint discovery is the one soft spot — capture the endpoints once and the cloud is no longer needed. Cloud surface seen in the binary (app-side; nothing the pad itself contacts): API hosts service.urevosports.com and urevo.urevosports.com (HTTPS), H5 pages on h5.urevosports.com, plus two hardcoded plain-HTTP IP endpoints (http://106.52.219.41:8082, http://81.71.103.167 — Tencent Cloud ranges, likely legacy/fallback API hosts). OTA metadata comes from /product/api/ota/otaCheckVersion (plus getProductAll, addUpdateLog, addConnectLog) on the API host; workout/history sync under /data/api/ and the scale API under /api/service-scale/. All of it is account- bound app traffic — the BLE control plane never touches it.

credentials.notes: BLE-only control plane; no credentials cross the link and no authentication of any kind was found in the treadmill classes.

factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset procedure is recoverable from the app binary for the treadmills (the massager classes have a RestoreFactorySettingsResponse, treadmills do not). The pads hold no network credentials and no bonds, so there is nothing to clear for local control. Not stated rather than guessed.

methods.description: Connect over GATT. FTMS models: standard FTMS flow (subscribe 0x2ACD/0x2ADA, write Control Point 0x2AD9). FT models: enable notify on 0xFFF1, write Frame-A frames to 0xFFF2. UR models (URTM*/SYWP*): enumerate services, pick the write + notify characteristic pair, speak Frame-A (class 0x53) frames.

steps.action: Power on the pad so it advertises.
Scan: name prefixes URTM* / SYWP* (UR protocol), advertised service 0x1826 (FTMS) or 0xFFF0 (FT proprietary).
Connect over GATT and discover services; pick the protocol class by advertised service UUID (0x1826 / 0xFFF0) or name prefix.
Enable notifications (0x2ACD/0x2ADA on FTMS, 0xFFF1 on FT, enumerated notify char on UR), then write commands (0x2AD9 / 0xFFF2 / enumerated write char).
steps.expect: Status notifications arrive; speed commands change belt speed. NOT yet confirmed on hardware.

setup.notes: No provisioning, pairing or bonding is visible in any treadmill code path of the official app: scan, connect over GATT, enable notifications and write commands. Confidence medium rather than high: this rests on static analysis only — no bonding/pairing API usage exists in the treadmill classes, but no hardware capture has confirmed the pads accept an unbonded central.

rejoin.notes: The pad joins no network. Any client may connect once the previous central disconnects (single-connection peripheral, as typical for this device class — not yet confirmed for UREVO hardware).

request_control.description: Standard FTMS Request Control (opcode 0x00). Assumed from FTMS 1.0; not yet confirmed as emitted by the app.

set_target_speed.description: Standard FTMS Set Target Speed (opcode 0x02), uint16-LE in 0.01 km/h. Assumed from FTMS 1.0; not yet confirmed as emitted by the app.

start_or_resume.description: Standard FTMS Start or Resume (opcode 0x07). Assumed from FTMS 1.0.

stop_or_pause.description: Standard FTMS Stop or Pause (opcode 0x08, param 0x01 stop / 0x02 pause). Assumed from FTMS 1.0.

characteristics.name: Treadmill Control Point
characteristics.notes: Write target for FTMS commands; responses parsed as standard control-point responses with result codes, per FTMS 1.0. Exact opcodes emitted by the app not yet extracted from the Dart AOT code — standard FTMS 1.0 opcode set expected (needs HCI snoop).

characteristics.name: Treadmill Data
characteristics.notes: Standard FTMS Treadmill Data; parsed by the app's shared FTMS reader. No vendor flag extensions found in the binary.

characteristics.name: Fitness Machine Status
characteristics.notes: Standard FTMS status events; in the class's notify-characteristic list.

characteristics.name: Training Status
characteristics.notes: In the class's notify-characteristic list (0x2AD3 = Training Status per FTMS 1.0).

characteristics.name: Supported Speed Range
characteristics.notes: Read by readSupportSpeedRange after connect; use it to bound speed commands per model.

characteristics.name: Supported Inclination Range
characteristics.notes: Read by readSupportInclinationRange; relevant on incline-capable models.

services.name: Fitness Machine Service (FTMS-generation models)
services.notes: Standard Bluetooth FTMS, selected when the advertisement carries 0x1826. The full characteristic set below is confirmed by the handler's UUID accessors in the app (each UUID string is referenced by the accessor for the corresponding characteristic). No vendor extension, pre-amble or private characteristic was found in this path — unlike KingSmith's FTMS generation, there is no ODM characteristic and no supplement service. Command frames are built in code (no constant FTMS frames embedded); assume standard FTMS 1.0 Control Point semantics (0x00 Request Control, 0x02 Set Target Speed with uint16-LE 0.01 km/h, 0x07 Start/Resume, 0x08 Stop/Pause) until an HCI snoop confirms the exact opcode set the app emits.

characteristics.name: Status / response notifications
characteristics.notes:
Inbound proprietary frames. Responses are dispatched on a key built from the protocol handler plus the frame's command class and sub-command bytes; treadmill answers carry the same cmd class as the request. Full treadmill mapping recovered from that dispatch table:

  51   (no sub) -> status report
  53 01 -> prepared/ready ack   53 02 -> set-speed-and-slope ack
  53 03 -> stop ack             53 04 -> BLE-link state report
  53 09 -> start ack            53 0A -> pause ack
  50 00 -> version info         50 02 -> speed configuration
  50 03 -> slope configuration
  50 04 -> mileage / odometer
  53 10 -> dot-matrix screen contents  (UR class only)
  53 11 -> dot-matrix screen write ack (UR class only)
  10 01 -> OTA major version            (Frame-B frame)

The FT and UR treadmill classes share this map: the keys are namespaced per handler but resolve to the same parsers. Keys 50 00 (version info), 50 04 (mileage), 53 04 (BLE-link state), and the dot-matrix pair have no matching command builder in the UR path — either unsolicited / model-specific, or their builders are inlined elsewhere; treat as response-only until a sender is confirmed. Per-field offsets inside these responses are not yet recovered — parsing lives in the per-handler parse routine; needs an HCI snoop or further disassembly.
Command class 0x40 (previously "purpose unidentified") is a different product family: keys 4000-4004 map to parsers for light set/get, switch-config get/set and an electrical-usage query — a lighting/electrical accessory, not a treadmill.

ft_prepared.description: FT class: prepare/ready the belt before a workout.

ur_get_controller_version.description: UR class: query controller (OTA-major) version — a Frame-B frame: header fields 01 03 00, cmd 0x10 sub 0x01, data length 0, CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over bytes 0-8 appended little-endian. The answer is the OTA-major-version report. The massager V2 handler emits the identical frame.

ur_get_equipment_status.description: UR class: poll current equipment status — cmd 0x51 with NO sub-command byte. The answer is the status report.

ur_get_slope_config.description: UR class: query slope configuration — cmd 0x50 sub 0x03. The answer is the slope-configuration report.

ur_get_speed_config.description: UR class: query speed configuration (range/step) — cmd 0x50 sub 0x02. The answer is the speed-configuration report.

ur_set_speed_and_slope.description: UR class: set target belt speed and slope. Speed and slope are integer counts of the device-reported step (see service notes); slope 0 on flat models.

slope.description: Target incline in device slope-step counts; 0 on flat walking pads. Defaults to 0 so a speed-only client can drive set-speed without owning an incline it does not have.

speed.description: Target speed in device speed-step counts (display speed / step). Absolute step TBD from the speed-config response.

ur_training_pause.description: UR class: pause, belt holds state.

characteristics.name: Command write
characteristics.notes:
All commands below are Frame-A frames; checksums on the constant commands are shown resolved per the formula above. Every byte sequence here was recovered by disassembling the app's command builders — none of it has been exercised against real hardware yet.
The UR class's controller version-info query is a Frame-B frame and is now fully recovered — see ur_get_controller_version below. CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over the first 9 bytes is 0x6F8C, appended little-endian. The answer is the OTA-major-version report (cmd 0x10 sub 0x01), NOT the Frame-A version info that answers cmd 0x50 sub 0x00.

services.name: Proprietary frame service (FT class; UR class endpoint TBD)
services.notes:
Private 16-bit service 0xFFF0, write 0xFFF2, notify 0xFFF1 — the FT handler's service, write-characteristic and notify-characteristic accessors reference exactly these UUIDs. This is the endpoint for the FT class, which also covers that family's exercise bikes. The UR class (name prefixes URTM*/SYWP*) speaks the SAME frame grammar — identical builder and serialiser code — but no UUID constants exist in the binary for it, so its GATT endpoints must come from hardware capture; the UR command set is documented here because the wire grammar is shared.
Frame A frame grammar (both directions; recovered from the frame builder, the frame factory and the checksum helper):

  02 <cmd> <sub> <payload...> <checksum> 03

- byte 0 = 0x02 (frame start; the frame factory dispatches on
  first == 0x02 AND last == 0x03)
- byte 1 = command class (0x44 FT equipment, 0x53 UR treadmill,
  0x50 config query, 0x51 status query; 0x40 also exists, purpose
  unidentified)
- byte 2 = sub-command / action (optional; absent on the 0x51
  status query)
- payload = zero or more parameter bytes - checksum = (cmd + sub + sum(payload bytes)) & 0xFF, then XOR 0x5A
  (disassembly of the checksum helper: additive sum of the command
  class, the sub-command and every payload byte, masked to 8 bits,
  XOR 0x5A)
- last byte = 0x03 (frame end)
A second frame family, Frame B, carries version/OTA traffic. Its full layout is recovered (the builder, serialiser, parser and CRC helper):

  5A A5 <f1> <f2> <f3> <cmd> <sub> <len u16-LE> <data...> <crc u16-LE>

- bytes 0-1 = 0x5A 0xA5 (the frame factory dispatches on these) - f1/f2/f3 = three 1-byte header fields (0x01 0x03 0x00 in the
  version query; semantics unidentified — possibly
  protocol-version/type constants)
- cmd/sub = the command key (0x10 0x01 = controller version query;
  answers are dispatched on the same cmd/sub pair, so 0x10 0x01 in
  equals the OTA-major-version report out)
- len = uint16 little-endian count of data bytes
  (built from a native 16-bit list view, i.e. ARM little-endian)
- crc = CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, MSB-first, no
  final XOR) over ALL preceding bytes including the 5A A5 header,
  appended little-endian. The inbound parser recomputes it and
  rejects on mismatch; minimum accepted frame length is 11 bytes.

Frame-B response keys seen in the app's response dispatch: 1001 -> OTA major version (treadmill and massager V2); 1002/1003/1004 -> OTA update start / write / exit (massager V2 only — no treadmill OTA-push commands exist in this app version).
Speed/slope encoding: the set-speed-and-slope builder converts the display speed via the app's km/h conversion (slope via the symmetric inverse), which divide by a per-unit factor read from a runtime unit-config map (keys 'kmh' / 'slope', default 1.0 when unset). The absolute speed step (0.1 km/h or otherwise) is therefore not a fixed constant in the binary — read it from the 0x50 speed-config response on hardware.

services.name: Device Information Service
services.notes: Standard DIS, parsed by the app's BlueDIS class. Characteristic strings 0x2A23-0x2A29 (system ID, model number, serial number, firmware revision, hardware revision, software revision, manufacturer name) are all referenced by getters. The model-number string is the likely per-model key the app feeds into its config/factory routing.
